curation_note: Primary, maintained, practitioner-useful sources. Inclusion is not endorsement or proof of compliance.

resources.title: AI Risk Management Framework
resources.why: The most reusable vendor-neutral backbone for enterprise AI risk work.
resources.use: Select Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage outcomes that fit the system and retain evidence for each decision.

resources.title: AI RMF Playbook
resources.why: Turns the AI RMF outcomes into candidate actions and evidence.
resources.use: Use as a menu and tailor; do not copy every action into an undifferentiated checklist.

resources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
resources.why: A concise, authoritative treatment of GenAI-specific risks and actions.
resources.use: Map applicable actions into design review, evaluation, supplier review, monitoring, and incident response.

resources.title: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 — Artificial intelligence management system
resources.why: The international certifiable management-system standard for AI.
resources.use: Use for management-system rigor, internal audit, supplier expectations, or certification scope.

resources.title: ISO/IEC 42005:2025 — AI system impact assessment
resources.why: Provides a repeatable process for assessing AI system impacts throughout the lifecycle.
resources.use: Align the impact-assessment workflow and evidence model while retaining jurisdiction-specific assessments.

resources.title: OECD AI Principles
resources.why: A globally influential policy baseline with common language for trustworthy AI.
resources.use: Use as executive principles, then translate each principle into owners, controls, tests, and evidence.

resources.title: OECD Framework for the Classification of AI Systems
resources.why: Gives consistent dimensions for describing context, data, models, tasks, and impact.
resources.use: Adopt its dimensions in inventory and risk-tiering fields to reduce ambiguous classification.

resources.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 — Artificial Intelligence Act
resources.why: The authoritative legal text for the EU's horizontal AI regime.
resources.use: Determine territorial scope, role, system category, applicable dates, and obligations with qualified counsel.

resources.title: EU AI Act Service Desk
resources.why: The Commission's official implementation hub, including an explorer and compliance checker.
resources.use: Use for orientation and official materials; validate conclusions against the law and legal advice.

resources.title: AI Controls Matrix v1.1
resources.why: A detailed vendor-neutral AI control catalog with useful framework mappings.
resources.use: Crosswalk existing cloud, security, privacy, and risk controls before creating AI-specific duplicates.

resources.title: Guidelines for Secure AI System Development
resources.why: A lifecycle security baseline backed by multiple national cybersecurity agencies.
resources.use: Put its requirements into engineering gates, architecture review, supplier due diligence, and operations.

resources.title: Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI
resources.why: The strongest concise government framework focused specifically on governing agents.
resources.use: Apply its four dimensions to responsibility, technical controls, lifecycle controls, and end-user responsibility.

resources.title: Careful Adoption of Agentic Artificial Intelligence Services
resources.publisher: Cyber Centre Canada and international partners
resources.why: A joint national-security-agency baseline for adopting agents without uncontrolled exposure.
resources.use: Start with constrained pilots, least privilege, action monitoring, containment, and recovery.

resources.title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026
resources.why: An actionable threat taxonomy for systems that plan, call tools, delegate, and act.
resources.use: Map each applicable threat to prevention, a test case, a detection signal, and a response owner.

resources.title: Agentic AI Addendum to the Australian Government AI Technical Standard
resources.why: An unusually concrete set of agent lifecycle control statements.
resources.use: Reuse criteria for memory, orchestration, evaluation, observability, shutdown, and accountability.

resources.title: MITRE ATLAS
resources.why: An evidence-based knowledge base of adversary tactics and techniques for AI-enabled systems.
resources.use: Build threat models and red-team scenarios from techniques relevant to the deployment.

resources.title: Adversarial Machine Learning: A Taxonomy and Terminology of Attacks and Mitigations
resources.why: A precise common vocabulary for attacks, mitigations, and lifecycle stages.
resources.use: Normalize threat-model and test terminology across security, data science, and audit teams.

resources.title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025
resources.why: A practical baseline for common LLM application security failures.
resources.use: Convert applicable risks into architecture controls, misuse tests, and monitoring signals.

resources.title: Security Design Considerations for AI-Driven Automation Leveraging MCP
resources.why: Authoritative threat and design guidance for a fast-growing agent-tool connection surface.
resources.use: Apply to MCP server selection, identity, authorization, isolation, monitoring, and incident readiness.

resources.title: Model Context Protocol Security Best Practices
resources.why: Protocol-specific guidance for authorization, token, session, and confused-deputy risks.
resources.use: Make these practices acceptance criteria for MCP clients, servers, and gateways.

resources.title: Model Context Protocol Specification
resources.why: The normative source for how MCP clients and servers are expected to behave.
resources.use: Pin the implemented specification version and threat-model optional features and extensions.

resources.title: Agent2Agent Protocol Specification
resources.why: The normative source for cross-agent task and message interoperability.
resources.use: Document version, trust boundaries, identity propagation, task authorization, and artifact handling.

resources.title: Secure AI Framework: Focus on Agents
resources.why: A concrete agent-focused extension to a broader secure-AI framework.
resources.use: Compare its agent risks and controls with the deployment's threat model; verify controls independently.

resources.title: Secure AI Framework Controls
resources.why: An inspectable set of control objectives for secure AI engineering.
resources.use: Cross-reference engineering controls and retain independent assurance evidence.

resources.title: AI Data Security: Best Practices for Securing Data Used to Train and Operate AI Systems
resources.why: Directly addresses data poisoning, provenance, integrity, and operational data protection.
resources.use: Add controls to data pipelines, retrieval sources, model inputs, monitoring, and incident response.

resources.title: Coalition for Secure AI
resources.why: Open, practitioner-oriented workstreams on secure AI frameworks, supply chains, and preparedness.
resources.use: Track and reuse released taxonomies and controls where they fit your architecture.

resources.title: AI Incident Database
resources.why: Real incidents prevent risk workshops from relying only on imagined failures.
resources.use: Search analogous systems and convert relevant incidents into scenarios, controls, and tabletop exercises.

resources.title: OECD AI Incidents and Hazards Monitor
resources.why: A policy-oriented incident and hazard evidence source.
resources.use: Use trend and case evidence to refresh taxonomy, monitoring, and board reporting.

resources.title: Towards a Common Reporting Framework for AI Incidents
resources.why: Improves consistency of internal and external AI incident records.
resources.use: Align incident fields and classification so events can be compared and escalated.

resources.title: Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law
resources.why: The first binding international treaty focused on AI, human rights, democracy, and rule of law.
resources.use: Track national implementation and integrate rights, remedy, accountability, and public-interest analysis.

resources.title: HUDERIA — Risk and Impact Assessment of AI Systems
resources.why: A structured method centered on human rights, democracy, and rule-of-law impacts.
resources.use: Use for deployments with public, civic, rights, or high-impact consequences.

resources.title: Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
resources.why: A globally adopted normative baseline connecting AI to rights, environment, and social impacts.
resources.use: Use to widen impact analysis beyond technical performance and immediate users.

resources.title: Ethical Impact Assessment Tool
resources.why: An operational companion to UNESCO's AI ethics recommendation.
resources.use: Adapt questions to stakeholder engagement and broader social/environmental impact review.

resources.title: Artificial Intelligence: An Accountability Framework for Federal Agencies and Other Entities
resources.why: A concrete audit lens covering governance, data, performance, and monitoring.
resources.use: Use its questions to design internal audit scope and test evidence.

resources.title: The IIA's Updated AI Auditing Framework
resources.why: Connects AI risks with internal audit practice and the three-lines model.
resources.use: Define audit universe, assurance ownership, and risk-based engagements.

resources.title: AI and Data Protection Risk Toolkit
resources.why: One of the most actionable regulator-issued toolkits for AI privacy risk.
resources.use: Integrate applicable controls with DPIA, data governance, development, and procurement.

resources.title: Algorithmic Impact Assessment
resources.why: A transparent, field-tested questionnaire and risk-level model.
resources.use: Study and adapt its questions; do not assume its legal thresholds apply outside its scope.

resources.title: General-Purpose AI Code of Practice
resources.why: Official implementation material for GPAI provider obligations under the EU AI Act.
resources.use: GPAI providers should assess adherence with counsel; deployers can use it in supplier diligence.

resources.title: M-25-21: Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust
resources.publisher: US Office of Management and Budget
resources.why: The current US federal agency policy for AI governance and high-impact use.
resources.use: Federal teams should trace requirements to inventory, governance, risk management, and public reporting.

resources.title: M-25-22: Driving Efficient Acquisition of Artificial Intelligence in Government
resources.publisher: US Office of Management and Budget
resources.why: Connects AI risk and governance to federal acquisition practice.
resources.use: Federal buyers should incorporate its competition, data, rights, and risk requirements into acquisition plans.

resources.title: SR 26-2: Model Risk Management Guidance
resources.why: The current US banking model-risk guidance, superseding SR 11-7.
resources.use: Covered institutions should update policy references, scope, validation, governance, and evidence with counsel.

resources.title: Inspect AI
resources.why: A maintained open-source framework for reproducible model and agent evaluations.
resources.use: Version tasks, solvers, scorers, model settings, logs, and pass thresholds in CI or an evaluation pipeline.

resources.title: NIST Dioptra
resources.why: A NIST testbed for measuring and tracking AI risks with reproducible experiments.
resources.use: Use where its supported workflows fit; retain experiment configuration and artifacts as evidence.

resources.title: PyRIT
resources.why: A flexible open-source framework for automating generative-AI red-team workflows.
resources.use: Use only in authorized environments; define threat hypotheses, target scope, scoring, and remediation ownership first.

resources.title: garak — LLM vulnerability scanner
resources.why: An extensible scanner for known LLM failure and attack classes.
resources.use: Use as one test input, not a safety verdict; triage findings and add confirmed failures to regression suites.

resources.title: Project Moonshot
resources.why: An open toolkit for safety and security testing with practical attack modules.
resources.use: Select tests from the actual threat model and retain configurations and raw results.

resources.title: AILuminate Safety Resources
resources.why: Open safety benchmark methods and resources developed through a multi-stakeholder process.
resources.use: Use benchmark results as one evidence source and add deployment-specific scenarios and thresholds.

resources.title: AILuminate Agentic AI Safety
resources.why: A focused effort to develop repeatable agent safety evaluations.
resources.use: Track released scenarios and metrics; combine them with system-specific tool, identity, and recovery tests.

resources.title: Fairlearn
resources.why: A mature open toolkit for assessing and mitigating group fairness harms.
resources.use: Choose metrics from the harm model, analyze relevant slices, and document tradeoffs and uncertainty.

resources.title: AI Fairness 360
resources.why: A broad open-source collection of fairness metrics and mitigation algorithms.
resources.use: Use with domain and legal expertise; metric selection itself is a governance decision.

resources.title: Adversarial Robustness Toolbox
resources.why: A substantial library for testing and defending ML systems against adversarial attacks.
resources.use: Apply relevant attacks and defenses to supported model types in an authorized test environment.

resources.title: AI Explainability 360
resources.why: A varied set of explanation methods and supporting metrics.
resources.use: Test whether explanations are faithful, understandable, useful for the audience, and safe to disclose.

resources.title: promptfoo
resources.why: A practical evaluation and red-team runner that integrates readily with development workflows.
resources.use: Pin configuration, define objective assertions, review judge limitations, and gate releases on agreed tests.

resources.title: Giskard
resources.why: An open evaluation toolkit supporting ML and LLM application testing.
resources.use: Select tests from the impact and threat model; review generated findings before treating them as evidence.

resources.title: Evidently
resources.why: A widely used open-source option for evaluation reports and production monitoring.
resources.use: Define monitoring metrics and response thresholds from system risks, not from the tool's defaults.

resources.title: Open Policy Agent
resources.why: A mature general-purpose policy engine for enforceable authorization and configuration decisions.
resources.use: Externalize selected deterministic rules; version, test, review, and fail safely.

resources.title: Cedar Policy Language
resources.why: A purpose-built authorization policy language suitable for fine-grained access decisions.
resources.use: Use for explicit principal-action-resource-context rules and test deny-by-default behavior.

resources.title: OpenTelemetry Generative AI Semantic Conventions
resources.why: A standards-based route to portable telemetry for model and agent operations.
resources.use: Adopt appropriate spans/events while minimizing sensitive content and preserving action/approval lineage.

resources.title: CycloneDX Machine Learning Bill of Materials
resources.why: Extends bill-of-materials practice to ML models, datasets, and related components.
resources.use: Generate and retain component inventories for higher-risk builds and supplier artifacts.

resources.title: C2PA Technical Specification
resources.publisher: Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity
resources.why: The key open technical standard for cryptographically bound content provenance.
resources.use: Evaluate for media workflows; communicate what provenance can and cannot prove.

resources.title: Data Cards Playbook
resources.why: One of the most usable guides for documenting datasets and stakeholder needs.
resources.use: Adapt its workflow and questions to data review, provenance, limitations, and handoffs.

resources.title: A Practical Guide to Building AI Agents
resources.why: A clear engineering treatment of when agents fit, orchestration, tools, and guardrails.
resources.use: Use for architecture questions, then assess the implementation with vendor-neutral controls and tests.

resources.title: Demystifying Evals for AI Agents
resources.why: A detailed practical guide to the distinct challenges of evaluating agent trajectories and outcomes.
resources.use: Use to design suites, graders, transcripts, and iteration; independently validate safety claims.

resources.title: Introduction to the NIST AI RMF 1.0 — Explainer Video
resources.why: A short authoritative orientation suitable for stakeholder onboarding.
resources.use: Assign before a workshop, then apply the framework to a real system rather than stopping at awareness.

resources.title: Designing Reliable Agent Architectures
resources.why: A production-focused treatment of reliable agent architecture.
resources.use: Use for engineering education and convert architecture ideas into explicit controls and evaluations.

resources.title: Evals: The Key to Production-Ready AI Apps
resources.why: A practical orientation to evaluation-driven AI application development.
resources.use: Pair it with a written evaluation plan, representative data, release thresholds, and retained evidence.
